en: Friend, who is it, alas, that comes and turns away every day?
Give him one blossom from my hair.
If he asks who gave it, in what flower garden—
By my oath, do not speak my name.
The one I have loved with all my heart,
can she turn me away, friend?
I dwell outside the world;
I do not know what happens in the world.
Who knows—here, the one a soul longs for with all its life,
whether it wins that one or not (I do not know),
so I have come, trembling with fear,
to the door of an unknown heart.
I love everything of yours—
that wealth of beauty,
that play, that song, that honeyed smile.
With these you have covered all my life—
where is your limit, within this world?
Who are you, and why do you tell your longing to my friend?
Who wants to know whether you love or love not?
The moon laughs, the evening laughs, the grove blooms with flowers,
youth laughs, blossoming in the heart's spring.
Why do you sigh, why do you not laugh?
Have you come to break up the play,
this fair of hearts among friends?
Take away your own sorrow, your own shadow.
Stand aside from life's road of joy.
From afar offer your worship at the lotus-throne of the heart.
Then be happy, be happy. I go—I go.
Friend, call her; there is no use in false play.
Do not be impatient, friend;
no one returns when hope is sated; keep hope alive and they return.
I was alone in my own world—where have I come now?
I do not know the paths here; I turn back.
If only I could find again that house of rest.
Friend, call her back. No use in false play, in false disdain.
Do not be impatient, friend;
no one returns when hope is sated; keep hope alive and they return.
I have lost my whole world.
The melody of the world's vina falls silent.
My homeless heart goes down a lightless road, alas—
I descend into the depths of a cave of dense darkness.
In your eyes is the light of the evening star;
kindle it, kindle it in the darkness of my road.
Chasing after mirages, my thirst-scorched hours have passed in vain.
At day's end, in your heart alone,
this weary traveler journeys to the shrine of immortality.
Do not err, oh, do not err—do not
err in love.
Do not beguile me, do not beguile me, do not beguile me with fruitless hope.
I live with the sorrow of parting; it never plays me false—
I know its language well.
Do not be cruel under the guise of kindness.
Do not break a heart while offering your heart.
Do not keep me craving—entrancing me with death's flute,
do not drag me into ruin.
I had erred; the error is shattered.
Now I have woken, I have known—
now no more error, no more error.
I wandered chasing after illusion;
I have known that dreams are all false.
The thorn of desire has pierced my soul—
this is no flower, no flower!
If I win love I will not slight it,
I will not play games with a heart.
In that love-filled soul I will take shelter, friend—
this world is a fathomless sea;
this is no shore, no shore!
The bee turns away again and again,
the bee comes back again and again.
Only then does the flower bloom.
The bud longs to open and does not open; it dies of shame, it dies of dread.
Forget pride and slight; give heart and soul; stay near, night and day.
Oh, give up hope, and yet keep hope alive,
in hope of the heart's jewel.
Come back, come back; the wood is drunk with the scent of flowers.
Tonight, in this night of parting, the full-blown blossoms float in waters of dew.
Do not call me, do not call—do not call.
Do not keep in your heart one who has walked away.
I have brought my pain away with me;
I ask no price for having loved.
Do not look back from the corner of your eye with a crumb of pity.
The flood-tide current of my sorrow
will carry me away from all humiliation.
When I have moved far away, then you will know me—
do not cover your neglect with pretence.
Not understanding, whom have you drowned in tears?
Oh, who is gazing down the empty road,
whose life is without joy, whose soul burns?
You never read the language of someone's eyes,
you never understood the hope of someone's heart,
you never looked back—
you have come trampling the longing of an anxious soul.
She who walked in my dreams—
her I could not understand;
my days have passed in searching and searching.
In a blessed hour you called me near, you covered my shame—
you I could understand with ease.
Who will turn me away in neglect, who will call me near,
in the pain of whose love do I have worth—
I can struggle no more with this endless doubt.
You alone I have been able to understand.
Alas, luckless woman,
your boat drifted in vain on the current; it never reached the shore, never reached it.
You spent your day tuning the vina—
at a harsh pull it broke out weeping;
on the snapped string the melody fell silent.
He came to this roadside and called you.
You turned him away at your barred door.—
My heart has burned—yet why did I never beg forgiveness?
Come, come, Spring, to the earth.
Bring the cuckoo's call, songs of love;
bring the languid breeze heavy with fragrant wine;
bring the surge of new youth, new life,
blossoming young desire to the earth.
Come, trembling and quivering, murmurous with rustling,
thrilled with new leaves,
into the bower of malati vines restless with flowers,
in happy shade, on honeyed breeze—come, come.
Come to the lap of young dawn with her crimson lotus feet.
Come in the moonlight-swooning midnight,
on the bank of the murmuring, rippling river,
on the lake's waters happily asleep—come, come.
Come into hearts aching with youth,
come into eyes languid with the joy of union,
come into the midst of sweet shyness,
bind arm to arm,
and with bonds of new blossoms weave a new bond of union.
Has she come, or has she not come—
it cannot be told, cannot be told.
Is she illusion, or a dream's shadow—is she deception?
Can she be caught in the noose of beauty?
Will the strains of song bind her?
She is the quest of eternal separation.
What plaintive note sounds on her flute
in a mode where parting and union mingle.
In joy or sorrow, she is the won and the unwon,
in the heart's forest she is a listless wind—
perhaps she is only the ultimate desire.
Is this a dream! Is this illusion!
Is this Pramada! Is this Pramada's shadow!
What errant storm shook down this flower,
just as the bud had first unfolded its young sweetness?
The star of the new morning
has lost its way at evening.
This was an earring of a celestial maiden of Amaravati.
This is a treasure fit to grace a crown—
alas, if any tender soul remains, touch it to your head.
Shall it drift away on the current to a far, pitiless land—
I do not know—who knows where, at day's end, it will find a shore.
Shame, shame—I die of shame.
Who decked me in false array?
Fate's cruel mockery brought me, softly, softly,
between the two of you.
I am not here, I am not here—
beloved, take your place where your throne stands.
At this blessed hour of union let the flute sound;
let laughter wake in a cloudless sky.
Through so much sorrow, so far and far, wandering the sea of darkness,
the golden boat has floated to the shore.
O maidens of the house, bring the welcoming tray adorned.
In the great festival of the couple's union, with the blessed conch's sound,
let spring's joy overflow.
No more, no more.
Why does the spring breeze still blow over withered flowers?
The auspicious hour has drifted by, taking every hope—
what lamp is this you light! It scorches my breast.
My garden has turned to desert—
in this evening darkness, what flowers do you gather there?
From whose destiny do you steal the bridal garland—
filling a broken basket?
Can my throat still bear the thorn-weight of the union garland?
With the broken chain on your feet, O bird,
fly away, fly away, go alone.
That fetter will clink at your feet, but your wings will find joy—
the wayless cloud has passed, calling you.
In pure sorrow lies that freedom, in love of the pure void.
Self-mockery is a terrible shame; let it cease utterly.
In the half-death of vain hope you lived so long in your cage—
go now, leaving it in the dust.
Let it tear, let the net of falsehood tear away.
Today, in the palace of sorrow, the hour of freedom has come.
This is well, oh, this is well—the light of separation's flame.
Let cruel truth grant, grant its boon—let the veil of deception fall away.
Go, beloved, go, go on your chariot of victory. I will not bar your way.
Before you take your leave, may your heart wake from its dream—
let all the clutter be made pure.
The love born in the blazing sacrificial fire of sorrow
is radiant gold—
eternal, beyond doubt; its glory is imperishable.
Beyond vain longing it dwells at the shrine of separation,
where eternal despair burns in the restless flame of the sacrificial fire;
free from thirst's burning, it stays unstained day after day.
Its glory is imperishable—
an ascetic bathed in the waters of the fountain of tears, conqueror of death.
Come, today play the game of breaking the game.
Come, tear down the nest of happiness.
The bond of the union garland will snap,
today the dream of Phalgun days will scatter—
come, spread the wings of a soaring mind.
On that peak of the sunset mountain
the storm-cloud's banner flies today.
The Kalbaisakhi storm will have its dance—
let your death-and-life dance along with it,
come, kick aside laughter and weeping.
